name: Alumni Chapel — small current-campus study
scope: Chapel and its immediate grounds only; expansion requires visual acceptance
coordinate_system: VoxelEarth local metres: X east, Z south; local v follows the nave toward the southern entrance

evidence.supports: Architect SP-1 graphic scale gives approximate 19.6 m transverse width and 7.7 m depth of proposed southern addition, with entrance steps projecting a further 4–5 m.
Original footprint, nave axis, ground elevation, approximately 10 m nave ridge and 17 m tower above its base
Current south gable, entrance arch, large traceried upper window, pale surrounds, buttresses, iron railings, copper lanterns
Brownstone masonry, stone tracery, copper flashings, asphalt replacement roof, eastern open arcade, square tower with slotted parapet and separate crenellated turret
2023 proposed addition is on the southern side and has area 1,445 square feet

uncertainties: The addition is approximately 19.6 by 7.7 metres from GKO's scaled proposed SP-1 plan, with about 1 metre raster-reading uncertainty. Confirm against the built geometry before acceptance.
Facade opening sizes and rhythm are manually interpreted from photographs, not a measured architectural survey.
Ordinary stone-brick blocks use a local original brownstone pixel-art texture. This is a material interpretation, not a scanned texture; vanilla without the pack shows gray masonry.

Major tree crowns are inferred from unclassified LiDAR geometry and checked against broad planting masses on SP-1; species, trunk positions and fine crown shapes remain interpretations. Crown surfaces are smoothed at 1 metre and incomplete crop-edge trees are omitted.
Asphalt has no literal vanilla block; polished deepslate and matching slabs/stairs use the vanilla gray-concrete texture through local model definitions, preserving measured terrain elevations.

Smooth sandstone components use an original generated cut-brownstone albedo. The small metal clock and pale louver blades use explicit reserved trapdoor states and original JSON component models in the dedicated pack; they revert to trapdoors without this pack.
Beds and low shrubs follow visible front/east planting zones; their individual plant species and positions are interpreted rather than surveyed.
